method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reconstruction of both directions of the language-change operation, replay of the same-domain and common-interpretation definition, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Reducts and expansions of structures under language inclusion, invariance of old-language sentences, and notation for expanding a structure by one interpreted predicate.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: When L is included in L-prime, an L-structure can be expanded by interpreting the extra symbols while retaining the common interpretations, and an L-prime structure can be reduced by forgetting those extra interpretations. The formal pair has one domain and agrees on every L constant, function and predicate.
samples.checks: Language inclusion, both operation directions, the same-domain clause and all three common-symbol interpretation clauses are retained without turning a reduct into a substructure.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If M is the L-reduct of M-prime, every L-sentence has the same truth value in both structures. The source leaves the proof as an exercise and immediately asks the reader to prove the proposition.
samples.checks: The universal sentence scope, satisfaction biconditional, exercise-only proof and exact proposition reference are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If L-prime adds one n-place predicate P to L and R is an n-place relation on M's domain, M-bracket-R denotes the expansion M-prime that interprets P as R.
samples.checks: The one-symbol language extension, predicate arity, relation power, expansion notation and assignment equation are exact.
